articles.title: Bath go top with Finn Russell to the fore in thrilling derby victory against Exeter
articles.summary: Prem Rugby: Bath 40-34 Exeter. Hosts made to fight all the way in 11-try thriller. Bath went to the top of the Prem after beating Exeter Chiefs in a pulsating West Country derby at the Rec but they were made to fight all the way in an 11-try thriller.
body: Exeter trailed 26-10 at the interval but rallied to lead 33-31 midway through the second half before a yellow card for scrum-half Stephen Varney eventually proved decisive.

Cam Redpath, Dan du Preez, Bernard van der Linde, Ted Hill and Finn Russell scored Bath’s tries. There was also a penalty try award with Russell converting four. The hugely impressive Immanuel Feyi-Waboso scored two tries for Exeter, with Jack Yeandle, Josh Iosefa-Scott and Varney also going over. Henry Slade converted three and Harvey Skinner added a late penalty.

Bath’s director of rugby, Johann Van Graan, was delighted with another five points. “We wanted to start well and achieved this to build up a healthy first-half lead but they went on to dominate the third quarter,” he said.

“We then brought on our bench and obviously they made a big impact, so we finished strongly to get a valuable five points. It was particularly pleasing to see Jaco Coetzee back in action. He’s been out for nearly two years and he and Will Stuart, who also returned, made a big impact.
points: Hosts made to fight all the way in 11-try thriller.

articles.title: Nations League: Italy earn draw against 10-man France, Northern Ireland stun Ukraine
articles.summary: League A: France 1-1 Italy, Belgium 3-0 Turkey. Northern Ireland boost promotion bid with 3-0 win. Zinedine Zidane’s first home game in charge of France ended with a 1-1 draw against Italy in the Nations League on Friday.
body: Michael Olise put France ahead in the 55th minute with a curling shot that went in off the crossbar, following a short free-kick taken by Rayan Cherki. But poor defending midway through the second half allowed Italy defender Alessandro Bastoni to run through and clip a low shot inside the right post.

Moise Kean missed a close-range chance early on for Italy, shooting straight at goalkeeper Mike Maignan. Donnarumma made a double save from Ousmane Dembélé and Désiré Doué early in the second half, then produced a brilliant low save to deny Adrien Rabiot moments after Italy’s equaliser.

Upamecano was sent off late in the game for picking up a second yellow card, but the hosts kept pushing for a winner, and Donnarumma had to claw away Eduardo Camavinga’s shot in stoppage time to preserve a point.

“We would have liked to win for our fans tonight but I was obviously really touched and delighted to be back at the Stade de France,” Zidane said afterwards. “I am happy with the performance albeit not with the result. We had chances to score a second goal and we didn’t do it. But I am really proud of my players.”

Northern Ireland boost promotion bid with 3-0 win.

articles.title: Pretorius breaks Gayle's T20 record score
articles.summary: Lhuan-dre Pretorius breaks Chris Gayle's record for the highest score in a men's T20 match with an unbeaten 188 in a domestic fixture in South Africa.
body: The 20-year-old South African's knock off 79 deliveries, including 13 sixes and 15 fours, helped Titans post 267-3 against Knights in the CSA T20 Challenge.
It eclipsed the 175 made by Gayle for Royal Challengers Bangalore (now Bengaluru) against Pune Warriors in the 2013 Indian Premier League.
Pretorius, who has played 17 T20s, three one-dayers and two Tests for South Africa, finished with a strike rate of 237.97.
He made his half-century off 24 balls but only required 16 more balls to get to three figures and then got to 150 off just 58 deliveries.

articles.title: Disgraced gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar removed from Michigan sex offender registry
articles.summary: Convicted offender among 20,000 people removed from list after state supreme court ruling on Sora registration law. Larry Nassar, the former Michigan State University and USA Gymnastics physician convicted of sexually abusing girls and women over a period of decades while claiming to provide…
body: Thousands of other offenders were also taken off that list after a court ruling involving how the state’s registration law can be applied.

On 9 September, the Michigan supreme court ruled that the state’s sex offender registration act (Sora) cannot be applied retroactively to cases involving offenses committed before the law’s relevant date. Michigan’s state police, as a result, removed more than 20,000 people whose offenses occurred before 1 July 2011 from the agency’s online sex offender database.

Nassar, 63, was among those removed. The Eaton county prosecuting attorney’s office – which was among the agencies to prosecute him – confirmed Nassar’s absence from the registry by sharing a screenshot showing a search for his name returning zero results.

“The Michigan supreme court’s decision to eliminate Sora requirements for these offenders is deeply concerning,” the attorney’s office said in a statement. “Our community, along with the victims of these crimes, expected the registry to provide a measure of protection and awareness – assurances that have now been removed by the court’s ruling.”

articles.title: Arsenal shelve plans for major expansion of Emirates Stadium
articles.summary: Club opt for improvements in hospitality and retail. An increase to 60,704 capacity had been considered. Arsenal have shelved plans for a major expansion of the Emirates Stadium, opting for a programme of smaller improvements as the club’s owners review the Premier League champions’ wider…
body: Arsenal set up a working group led by the chief executive, Richard Garlick, in 2024 to examine the feasibility of increasing the 60,704 capacity, with some reports they could temporarily hold home matches at Wembley. But the club has decided against major redevelopment and will concentrate on what it described as the “continued evolution” of their home since 2006.

Arsenal confirmed at a supporters’ meeting that improvements would focus on hospitality, retail, visitor facilities and the matchday experience – an area the co-chair Josh Kroenke previously highlighted.

“We shared a commitment to the continued evolution of Emirates Stadium, rather than a huge-scale masterplan, building on improvement we have made to date in partnership with our catering partner, Legends, the introduction of safe standing (this season in the Clock End, and next season in the North Bank), improving hospitality and retail experiences, and upgrading visitor experiences,” Arsenal said.

articles.summary: After an impressive 3-0 victory over Ukraine in the Nations League, Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill was impressed with his young side.
body: Michael O'Neill had spent the build-up to Northern Ireland's Nations League outing against Ukraine playing down memories of their famous win at Euro 2016.
His focus was firmly on what was to come rather than reflect on the past.
If a stunning 3-0 victory on Friday night was anything to go by, it's going to be a pretty exciting future indeed.
His starting team had an average age of just 22, which was the youngest on record for Northern Ireland since World War Two.

articles.summary: United States coach Mauricio Pochettino on Friday named Tyler Adams as his team's captain through to the 2030 World Cup. Pochettino, speaking ahead of the USA's friendly against Mexico in Arizona on Saturday, said Adams was the logical choice to lead the United States.
body: "I'm happy to announce and for everyone to know that he's going to be our leader and captain," Pochettino told reporters.
"We've had a very good relationship the last three years and I think he knows what I expect.
"He's a perfect role model for everyone in the way that he can translate the philosophy, the culture and represent (this) amazing country.
"He's the player that can lead the period that we have ahead."

articles.title: Trump whitewashes Selby to set up Wu semi-final
articles.summary: Judd Trump whitewashes Mark Selby at the Shenzhen Open to secure a semi-final tie against Wu Yize, who progresses to the last four after a thrilling victory over Shaun Murphy.
body: Trump notched five successive half-centuries against fellow Englishman Selby, but it was his composed safety play which helped him seal a 5-0 scoreline.
Selby had his chances in the first, third and fourth frames but was unable to compete with the world number two's cue-ball control.
World champion Wu made two centuries in the last three frames to edge a 5-4 victory over Murphy in a repeat of this year's Crucible final, which the Chinese player also won in a deciding frame.
Murphy had breaks of 104 and 98, but these came in between frames where he fluffed straightforward pots, allowing Wu to go into the interval on level terms.

articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers starter Tarik Skubal has been with the team for only two months, but he has earned the honor of starting Game 1 of the NLDS. Despite Yoshinobu Yamamoto being thought to be the Dodgers’ main starter, Skubal gets the ball first in a stacked rotation full of talent.
body: As the reigning two-time Cy Young Award winner, Skubal has the credentials to start the first game of the series, though he is not taking this opportunity for granted.

“Yeah, I mean, it’s an honor and a privilege to start Game 1 and have the trust of the coaching staff and my teammates and the organization to take the ball and go out there and do what I can do to put our team in a position to win,” Skubal said.
Skubal totaled 75 pitches in his last appearance against the San Francisco Giants on September 25th, throwing 60 strikes, racking up 10 punchouts, while allowing three hits and no walks.
He was dominant, and with that pitch count after seven innings, Skubal expected to shoot for a complete game.

articles.title: Italy earn draw at the Stade de France as Belgium win comfortably
articles.summary: On Zinedine Zidane 's return to the Stade de France, this time as coach, France drew 1-1 with Italy, leaving qualification for the next stage of the Nations League wide open. Michael Olise opened the scoring with a superb strike before Bastoni levelled 20 minutes from time.
body: After a balanced first half, with France holding a slight edge, Olise did what he does best in the 54th minute. Following a rehearsed free-kick routine, Rayan Cherki gave the ball a slight touch before the Bayern midfielder struck a powerful effort past Donnarumma. The ball clipped the bar on its way in to give France the lead.

Roberto Mancini 's side responded in the 67th minute. Bastoni took a risk pressing near the French penalty area and surprised Lucas da Cunha, winning possession before advancing and beating Mike Maignan to complete an excellent move.
Issa Doumbia came on for Italy in the 82nd minute. Five minutes later, Dayot Upamecano was sent off, leaving France with 10 men for the closing stages.
In the other group match, Belgium beat Turkey 3-0, leaving the visitors without a point after three games.

articles.title: Wade and Aspinall make statement ahead of World Grand Prix semi-finals
articles.summary: James Wade and Nathan Aspinall put in statement performances that will have made their semi-final opponents take note ahead of a mouthwatering Saturday night line-up at the World Grand Prix.
body: Aspinall threatened to set a new tournament record average when storming to a 3-0 win over Ryan Joyce, his 105.15 mark ultimately landing as the fourth-highest in history and the best-ever in a quarter-final.
Wade, meanwhile, dropped only one leg as he, in his words, "bashed up" world No 2 Gian van Veen in a match that lasted little more than 20 minutes.
"That really was a performance to remember from Wade," Sky Sports ' Wayne Mardle said. "From start to finish, he was absolutely devastating. World Class."
Three-time world champion John Part concurred with that assesment, saying: "James is not just looking like a great dart thrower to me, he's looking like a winner.

articles.title: 3 offensive keys for Ohio State against the Iowa Hawkeyes Saturday
articles.summary: Ohio State heads on the road for the second time this year and looks to avenge an early-season road loss to Texas by taking down top-15 Iowa on Saturday. It's been an inconsistent season thus far for the Buckeyes, with many highs but also some lows.
body: Iowa, who will host ESPN's College GameDay for the first time in 20 years, will also have its 32nd straight sellout. In an environment much like at Texas, Ohio State enters with a target on its back.
What are the offensive keys to the game for the Buckeyes, and what are some key questions they need to answer to come out on top? Let's dive in.

It's been a discussion point all season long; who steps up as wide receiver No. 2? Everyone knows what Jeremiah Smith brings to the table, and so do Iowa and Kirk Ferentz. With 33 catches, 617 yards, and seven touchdowns on the year, it's clear that Julian Sayin and this Ohio State offense will be seeking out Smith early and often, but Iowa seems to have a game plan in place to limit his production as much as possible.

articles.title: Brown scores twice as Northen Ireland cruise to win over Ukraine
articles.summary: Ciaron Brown's first international goals came as a pair to help a young Northern Ireland side stun Ukraine 3-0 and go clear at the top of Nations League Group B2.
body: Brown, the only player in Michael O'Neill's starting line-up over the age of 24, scrambled in early on before Isaac Price doubled the lead in the 22nd minute at the Stadion Antona Malatinskeho in Trnava, Slovakia.

Brown's second then came in bizarre fashion just after the hour - the 28-year-old Oxford defender went up to flick on Pierce Charles' free-kick from inside the Northern Ireland half and Ukraine goalkeeper Dmytro Riznyk let the bouncing ball through his legs.

On paper this was the hardest game in the group, away to a side ranked 37 places above Northern Ireland, but they brushed Ukraine aside to move on to seven points from their opening three games since returning to their second tier, still yet to concede going into Monday's game with Georgia in Belfast.

This was the first competitive meeting with Ukraine since Northern Ireland's famous 2-0 win at Euro 2016, and they delivered a performance which will have fans believing a major tournament beckons for this new generation.

articles.title: NFL London: 651-day wait over... Sauce's Colts go globe-trotting again
articles.summary: Sauce Gardner just ended a 651-day wait for an NFL win in the United States. Now the Indianapolis Colts cornerback is back on international soil.
body: The Colts clinched their first victory of the campaign in Week Three as they beat the Houston Texans 19-17, before which Gardner's last win in the U.S. came on December 15, 2024 during his time with the New York Jets.
Gardner was traded to the Colts in November 2025, his only win after that coming against the Atlanta Falcons in Berlin before Indianapolis lost their final seven games of the season.
He returns to Europe once again this week as the Colts face the Washington Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, live on Sky Sports NFL.

"The crazy thing I was saying to [team-mate] Josh Downs is imagine we had lost that game in the States, and then ended up playing international, win international but lose in the States. That was giving me a lot of pain," Gardner told Sky Sports.
